hyps.why: Adding a direct input-to-output skip where the edge was absent helps far more than replacing an existing conv or pool edge.
Filling an empty 0->3 edge with a conv adds a new path, while replacing a conv3x3 gives about zero gain.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to 1x1 loses capacity, whereas replacing a pool, skip or none edge with a conv gains.
Replacing a pooling input edge with a 3x3 conv gave smaller gains than replacing conv1x1, none or skip on this edge.
Removing a learned 3x3 conv hurts clearly, while removing a skip or pool edge is roughly neutral.
With edge 5 absent, edge 2's output cannot reach node 3 via node 2, so removing it is nearly harmless.
With edge 5 absent, upgrading edge 2 cannot influence the output through node 2, so the gain shrinks.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is dead and edge 2 carries no signal, so upgrading it gives little.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, edge 2 is already useless, so removing it costs almost nothing.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, edge 0 is a more critical route to the output, so removing it hurts more.
